title: One place for who owes what
bullets: A new Bills page under You adds up what you owe and what friends owe you, across all your circles.
Mark someone paid right there, or open the event to see who has paid.
Past events stay in the list until everyone has paid, so nothing slips away.

title: Hangry follows your light or dark setting
bullets: If your phone is set to light, Hangry is now light too. Dark phones look the same as before.
Menus, sheets, the calendar and the emoji picker all switch with it.
Plan cards and the map card stay dark so the pictures and colours still pop.

title: Smoother tabs, sheets and menus
bullets: Switching tabs now slides the new page in and gives the tab icon a small dip.
Sheets keep sliding down from where you let go when you drag them closed.
Card menus pop open and pop shut instead of blinking in and out.

title: The Goblin has more to say
bullets: The Goblin has more things to say when you @Goblin in chat, so replies vary more.
Your gripe is still filed as feedback, and the Goblin still asks what is wrong when you say nothing.

title: Send GIFs in chat
bullets: Tap GIF next to the message box to browse trending GIFs or search, then tap one to send it.
Tap GIF in a message's reaction bar to answer that message with a GIF.
GIFs come from Giphy and are kept to PG-13.

title: Set a price and see who has paid
bullets: Add a price per person in euros when you edit a plan or a free post.
Friends who are in get a PayPal link with the amount, or the Wero email with a copy button.
Everyone sees a Who paid list. The organizer or collector ticks it, and you can tick yourself.

title: Tap a chat title for the event details
bullets: In an event chat, tap the title at the top to see who is in and where, the same details as on the cards.
Close it and you are back in the chat, right where you were reading.

title: Pull down to refresh
bullets: Pull the Now, Events, Circle and You tabs down from the top to refresh them.
It works only at the top of the page, so scrolling a long list stays as it was.

title: React with any emoji in chat
bullets: Tap + at the end of the reaction bar to pick any emoji. You can search or browse by category.
The six quick reactions are still one tap away, and every reaction shows who picked it.

title: Tap links in chat and copy messages
bullets: Web links in a chat message are now tappable and open in a new tab.
Hold a message (or tap the smile on desktop) and choose Copy to copy its text.

title: Hangry now always uses the dark look
bullets: The app is dark on every device, so it is easy to read on desktop browsers in light mode.
Cards, chats and buttons that were hard to see in light mode look right again.

title: Sheets, titles and screens move like an app
bullets: Sheets stop halfway or open full. Flick one down to close it.
Now, Events, Circle and You have a big title that shrinks as you scroll.
Chat and Past events slide in, and slide back out when you go back.

title: Hangry feels more like an app
bullets: Buttons react the moment you touch them.
The tab bar is see-through, so the page shows softly behind it.
Tap the tab you are already on to jump back to the top.
Lists show a placeholder while they load instead of plain text.

title: Add your Wero email to your profile
bullets: Under You, Profile, you can add the email you use for Wero. It is optional.
Friends in your circle see it next to your name with a Copy button, so paying you back is quick.
It is separate from your sign-in email. Clear the box and save to remove it.

title: Add an email so you never get locked out
bullets: Every account now has an email. New accounts add one when they join, and existing accounts are asked once.
Lost your recovery code? We email you a sign-in link and make you a new code.
Your Flic button link and your recovery code are now separate. A new button link no longer changes your code.

title: Add a pay link to your profile
bullets: Under You, Profile, you can add your paypal.me link. It is optional.
Friends in your circle see a Pay link next to your name, so splitting a bill is one tap.
Only people who share a circle with you can see it. Clear the box and save to remove it.

title: A voluntary tip option
bullets: Hangry is free. You can now leave a small tip under You, Account. It is optional and never pops up.
The install prompt and the Donate button use a slightly deeper pink.
The new tip button only opens a PayPal link. Nothing is paid inside Hangry.

title: Faster loading, reliable updates
bullets: Hangry now opens faster, especially on a slow connection.
New versions reach your phone reliably, so you stop running an old copy.
Nothing changes in how the app looks or works.

title: Meet the Goblin
bullets: Type @Goblin in any chat, then say what bugs you. The Goblin files it as feedback.
It answers right in the chat so you know your gripe landed.

title: Invite links find your account
bullets: Opening an invite link on a device where you are signed out now offers I already have an account.
Enter your recovery code there and you sign in to your own account and join the circle in one step.
No more duplicate accounts when you tap an invite link from a chat.

title: Plan for this day is easier to find
bullets: In the Events calendar, Plan for this day is now a big pink button right under the day you picked.
You no longer have to scroll past the day's events to start a plan.

title: Pick the circle each Flic press posts in
bullets: With 2 or more circles, You > Account > Set up a Flic button lets you pick a circle for a single click, a double click and a hold.
Use one click for one circle and a double click for another. Each has its own link to copy.
Holding the button ends your social in the circle you chose for hold.

title: Plan from the calendar, and Back keeps your place
bullets: Pick a day in the Events calendar and tap Plan for this day to start a plan with that date filled in.
Back from an event, its chat or a place now returns you to where you were scrolled.
The plan note hint now suggests Amanda's inviting everyone for free tacos.

title: Event chats open again on a weak connection
bullets: Tapping an event chat now opens it right away, so the app no longer looks stuck when your signal is poor.
Slow requests give up after a short wait, and the chat fills in once your connection is back.

title: Admins can end events from the details
bullets: Open an event and circle admins and hosts now see an End button there, as well as in the ⋯ menu on the card.
When an admin ends someone else's hangout, it disappears for everyone and the host is told.

title: Install Hangry from You > Account
bullets: You > Account now has an Install app row. Tap it to add Hangry to your home screen, or to see the steps for your browser.
If Hangry is not installed, a small prompt shows when you open the app. Close it and it comes back next time you open Hangry.

title: Reading a chat clears its alerts
bullets: When you open a chat, that chat's alerts are marked read, so the dots on the bell and on those rows go away.
Alerts from other chats and events stay unread until you open the Alerts tab.

title: Long chat messages wrap
bullets: The message box now wraps long text onto new lines and grows as you type, instead of scrolling sideways.
Enter still sends. Shift+Enter starts a new line.

title: Clearer busy times
bullets: On See what friends see, each busy time now reads "Blocked from 09:00 to 10:00".
All-day blocks say "Blocked all day".

title: See what friends see
bullets: You > Availability & calendar has a new "See what friends see" page with your busy times by day.
It shows who they are shared with, and never any event names.
Spot a wrong block? Fix it in your calendar, then tap Check now.

title: Settings, split into pages
bullets: The You tab is now a short menu: Profile, Availability & calendar, Notifications, Assistants and Account.
Each section opens its own screen with a Back button, so nothing is buried in one long page.
The Android back button steps out of a section first, then leaves the You tab.

title: A public privacy policy
bullets: Hangry now has a privacy page at /privacy. It says what we store, including calendar and assistant tokens.
The login screen and the Google Calendar connect copy both link to it.
We do not show ads, and we do not sell your data. Ask in the app if you want your account deleted.

title: Google Calendar connects without a second login
bullets: After you connect Google Calendar, Hangry says it is connected as soon as you come back to the app.
If a browser page opens while you are not signed in, it tells you to go back to Hangry instead of asking you to log in again.

title: Get notified when friends react
bullets: When a friend reacts to your chat message, you get a notification.
It shows who reacted, which emoji, and a short bit of your message. Tap it to open the chat.
You are not notified for your own reactions, or when you have muted the chat.

title: Connect Google Calendar
bullets: Connect Google Calendar on the You tab so friends in circles you pick see when you're busy or free.
Hangry only sees busy times, never event names. The You tab says what is stored, how often it checks, and how to disconnect.
You can remove it in Hangry or revoke it at myaccount.google.com/permissions.
The private link still works. It includes event names, but Hangry keeps only the times and your own titles.

title: Busy until a time, or every week
bullets: On the You tab, tap 1 hour, 2 hours, Until 6pm or Until tomorrow to show Busy. It clears itself when the time is up.
Set weekly hours, like weekdays 9 to 5, and you show as Busy during them without lifting a finger.
Friends only see that you're busy or free, and until when. Never why.
Tell your circle you're free and it wins over Busy, so friends know they can reach you.

title: Let an assistant act for you
bullets: On the You tab, make a named token for an assistant. Copy it right away, it is shown only once. Revoke it any time.
With it, an assistant can read your circles, set your status, make plans and say you are in, as you.
Friends see those actions as you, so only share a token with an assistant you trust.

title: Tap to move the cursor while typing in chat
bullets: Tapping inside what you are typing in chat now moves the cursor, and the keyboard stays open.
Buttons and the rest of the app feel the same as before.

title: Faster map
bullets: The map stays dark until the dark map is ready, with no light street map flashing in first.
The app gets the map ready in the background, so opening it again feels snappier.
Pins, cards and the live buzz work just like before.

title: Mentions, reactions and replies in chat
bullets: Type @ in a chat to tag a friend. They get a notification that you mentioned them.
Press and hold a message to react with a quick emoji, or tap Reply. On a computer, use the smile or the arrow next to the time.
Reaction counts show under the message. Tap one to add or take back yours.
Swipe a message to the right to reply. A quote shows above what you write, and the person you replied to gets a notification.

title: Away or Busy
bullets: On the You tab you can set yourself to Away or Busy, with a short note, a place and an end day if you like.
Friends in your circles see a small badge on your picture and the note next to your name.
It clears itself after the end day, or you clear it yourself. You still get every buzz and plan.

title: Install Hangry after you join
bullets: After you join a circle from an invite, Hangry shows how to install it as an app on your phone.
On iPhone, open Hangry in Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
On Android, tap Install app, or use the Chrome menu and choose Install app.
Tap Not now to skip it. It does not come back every time you open Hangry.

title: See who's in on the card
bullets: Each card now shows the people who are coming, with their pictures and names.
People who can't make it are no longer listed on the card. Open the details to see them under Can't make it.

title: Dark map in Zürich too
bullets: The detailed dark street map now covers Zürich and the lake, the same way it already covers Stuttgart.
The stretch between the two cities is covered as well.
Outside this area you still see the regular street map. There is nothing to reinstall.

title: Alerts no longer repeat when you switch circles
bullets: Switching circles no longer pops up alerts you have already seen.
A new alert now shows once, even right after a few switches.
The Alerts list and the circle name stay on the circle you picked.

title: Say you're free with a Flic button
bullets: The You tab has a new Set up a Flic button section, with your button link and the steps for the Flic app.
One press tells your circle you're free now.
Holding the button can end your hangout again.

title: Share when you're free
bullets: Connect a private calendar link on the You tab.
Friends see only busy or free, never the names of your events.
You choose which circles see it. It stays off until you turn one on.
When you tap I'm in, you can check your own calendar for that day first.

title: Events: a monthly calendar and the map
bullets: The bottom tab is now called Events, with a calendar icon and a Map / Calendar switch at the top.
Calendar is the first view you see. After that, Events remembers whether you last picked Map or Calendar.
The month shows plans and hangouts, past days too, with the faces of who is in. Tap a day, then an event.
This circle / All circles works on the calendar the same way it works on the map, each circle in its own colour.

title: A clearer notification icon
bullets: On Android, the small Hangry icon in the status bar and on each notification is now a big solid dot, like the button in the app.
It was a faint blur before, so it is much easier to spot now.
Android draws that small icon in one colour. The pink Hangry dot still shows as the big picture inside each notification.

title: One map for every circle
bullets: If you are in more than one circle, the Map has a This circle / All circles switch at the top.
All circles puts every place from all your circles on one map, and remembers your pick.
A card on the All map names the circle it comes from, and In, chat and share go to that circle.

title: Nicer map pins
bullets: Each pin is now a small dark glass chip with the person's picture on the left.
The day and who is coming sit right inside the chip, next to the picture.
Someone free right now still pulses on the map. With Reduce motion on, the ring stays still.

title: Close the map card
bullets: A pin's card on the map now has an X in its corner to close it and get the whole map back.
Tapping an empty spot on the map or pressing Escape closes it too.

title: The dark map stays put
bullets: Dark map sticks while you look at the covered area, even if the edges stick out a little; zoom out past it and the usual map returns.
Pins, cards and the live buzz are unchanged.

title: A dark map, where we have one
bullets: The app can now draw a dark street map with German names, but only for an area the server has a map file for.
Until that file is set up you keep seeing the usual map, and outside its area you always do, with full detail.
Pins, cards and the live buzz work the same on both maps.

title: Smoother menus and tabs
bullets: The ⋯ menu on cards now opens with a quick, soft pop, and its items react when you press them.
Switching tabs fades the new page in gently. With Reduce motion on, both stay instant.

title: Livelier map pins
bullets: Plans on the map show their day under the pin, like Later today 19:00, Tomorrow or Sat 14 Nov.
Friends who are free right now buzz on the map so you spot them first.
Pins show profile photos, and a plan pin shows a small crowd of who is in.

title: Now and later first
bullets: Tap the red button and Now and Later today are the two main choices.
Pick a date is now the Plan for another day link below them. It works the same as before.

title: Tidier chat
bullets: Everyone's messages now start on the same line, so friends' messages no longer sit further in than yours.
Back, the message box and the text share one left edge. Times, Mute and Send share one right edge.

title: Reminders reach people who just joined
bullets: Joined a circle after someone tapped Remind friends? You no longer miss out. Anyone in the plan can remind you right away.
Everyone already reminded that hour is left alone, even if they cleared their Alerts.

title: Share plans anywhere
bullets: Tap Share on a plan card to send it to any chat or app on your phone.
The link shows only the title, day and time. Friends outside the circle can't see who's going or where.

title: Share a plan with more circles
bullets: Tap ⋯ on your plan and choose Share with other circles.
It stays one plan with one chat and guest list. Only the newly added circles get a notification.

title: Calendar feed on Android
bullets: Open in calendar did nothing on Android phones. The feed now shows Copy link and Send link with steps for Google Calendar.
On iPhone and Mac, Open in Apple Calendar still opens the calendar app.

title: Hear when your idea ships
bullets: Sent feedback that we built? You get an alert saying your suggestion is live, with a short quote of what you wrote.
Only you see it. It reaches you even if you have left the circle you sent it from.

title: Plans in your calendar
bullets: Tap ⋯ on a plan and choose Add to calendar to save it as a calendar file. That copy does not update.
Want it to stay in sync? Turn on Calendar feed on the You tab and add the private link to your calendar app.
Reset the link or turn it off any time. Your calendar app decides how often it checks for changes, which can take hours.

title: Nudge your friends
bullets: Tap ⋯ on a plan and choose Remind friends to send the notification again to people who have not answered yet or said maybe.
You can remind once an hour per plan.

title: Say maybe
bullets: Not sure yet? Open ⋯ on a plan and tap Maybe.
Friends see you're a maybe in Who's in.

title: More checks behind the scenes
bullets: We added checks so dates and places read the same in the app and in notifications.
Nothing changes for you.

title: Behind-the-scenes tidy-up
bullets: We removed old unused code from the app. Nothing changes for you.
Your plans, chats, and settings stay the same.

title: Sharper home-screen icon
bullets: On Android the Hangry icon now fills its shape, with no white frame around it.
If you still see the old icon, remove Hangry from your home screen and add it again.

title: One list, any day
bullets: Now shows everything in one list: who's free, then plans by day.
Tap the red button and choose Pick a date to plan something days ahead.

title: Red dot matches your alerts
bullets: Reading your alerts now clears the red dot on the circle too.
Unread chat keeps its own count on Chat, so it no longer keeps the circle dot on.

title: Buttons feel nicer
bullets: Buttons and cards give a small press when you tap them.
I'm in pops when you join. Reduce motion on your phone keeps it still.

title: Profile pictures
bullets: Add a photo on the You tab — friends see it on cards and in the circle.
No photo? Initials stay as they are.

title: Clearer place search
bullets: You'll see Searching… while places load, and a note if nothing turns up.
Enter in the place field searches — it no longer saves the plan.

title: Easier to tap who's in
bullets: Tapping "Waiting for friends" now opens the plan instead of the map.
The map only opens from the place with the pin.

title: Every plan has its own colour
bullets: Each plan card gets its own soft gradient, so you can tell them apart at a glance.
The colour stays the same on the map and in the plan's details.

title: Turn notifications off
bullets: You → Notifications now has a Turn off button.
This phone stops getting pushes. Turn them back on any time.

title: Clearer plan cards
bullets: One tap I'm in — tap again to undo. Hosts stay In.
Chat sits on the card with the last message and an unread badge.
Share, pick a time, Can't, Edit and End live under the menu.

title: Circle dots match Alerts
bullets: A red dot on a circle means that circle has unread alerts.
Open Alerts in that circle to mark them read — the dot clears.
Plan chats, new members and ended plans show up in Alerts too.

title: Back works like you expect
bullets: Tap the bell again to close Alerts. Your previous tab comes back.
The Back button closes sheets and panels instead of the app.

title: One plan, several circles
bullets: Hosts can share a plan with their other circles from Edit, under Also share with.
Everyone sees the same plan: one list of who's in and one chat.
A newly added circle gets one push. Circles that already had the plan stay quiet.

title: Heads-up when plans move
bullets: When a plan changes day, time or place, your circle gets a push. People who said they can't come are left alone.
The push shows the new date and time, like Fri 7 Nov · 20:00.
Fixing a typo in the title or description stays quiet.

title: Share a plan
bullets: Tap Share on a plan to send a link.
Friends in the circle open the plan straight away.
Anyone else only sees the title, day and time.

title: Plan description
bullets: Hosts can add a short description when they edit a plan.
It shows on the plan card and the map card. Tap to read more.
Changing only the description does not ping anyone.

title: What's new and feedback
bullets: New features show up here once, the first time you open the app after an update.
Open this list again any time from What's new in the You tab.
Send feedback from the You tab. It goes straight to the people building Hangry.
The Plan button now just says Plan, since plans can be for any day, not only tomorrow.

title: Your own colour
bullets: Everyone gets one colour that stays the same in every circle.
Your own messages show your colour as a bar along the side.
Avatars and map pins use the same colour.

title: Plans for any day
bullets: Make a plan for today, tomorrow or any date up to a year ahead.
Plans for today and tomorrow are under Today & tomorrow. Later ones are under Upcoming.
You can change the day when you edit a plan.

title: See who got your ping
bullets: Hosts see Delivered to X of Y under their post or plan.
Tap it to see each friend's status, like Delivered, Not installed or Notifications off.
Only the host sees this. Friends don't.

title: Smoother map editing
bullets: The Edit and End buttons on the map card no longer get in the way of the edit sheet.
The edit sheet stays above the keyboard while you type.
